messages.subject: morphol.disparity in phylogenetic context
parts:
Hi Geomorph folks,

I was reading a morphometrics paper this morning (Stayton et al. 2018, Evolution) and caught an interesting analysis that I would like to try out with my data. 

Stayton et al. were interested in comparing morphological disparity between two groups of turtles, aquatic and terrestrial. Terrestriality has apparently evolved multiple times from aquatic ancestors. Thus, the (paraphyletic) terrestrial group might be expected to show higher disparity simply due to their distribution on the tree. 

To account for the distribution of terrestrial taxa, Stayton et al. 1) calculated the ratio of aquatic to terrestrial disparity with the real data, 2) simulated shape evolution 999 times on the tree assuming a Brownian motion model of evolution 3) calculated the disparity of each simulated dataset 4) and then compared the distribution of disparities for the simulated data to the disparity of the real data.

I think it would be possible to re-use code from the compare.evol.rates function to do this with morphol.disparity, as compare.evol.rates seems to use a similar simulation procedure (when the method of simulation is chosen),  but I am having trouble interpreting the processing behind the compare.evol.rates function on the github.

Thus, my question is - how can I combine code snippets from the two functions (compare.evol.rates and morphol.disparity) to perform the analysis above?

Thank you,
Tony

parts:
Tony,

 

The answer is: you write your own function (see Introduction to R).

 

However, for your particular question, I believe Tristan has included that analysis as part of his ‘convevol’ R package. I recommend you begin there.


Dean
